title_en: Gao Ziyu v. Nanjing Metro Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over the right to health
ruling_gist_en: The duty of safety and security is a statutory obligation of the manager of a public place or public facility. The person bearing this duty must not only ensure the safety of the premises or facilities under its management, but also provide necessary warnings, instructions, notifications, and assistance to persons moving within the premises or using the facilities, so as to prevent harm. When a subway company uses automatic ticket gates to control passenger entry and exit, if it fails to make reasonable arrangements and management for fare-free passengers and their accompanying persons on how to safely pass through the gates, thereby causing a passenger to be injured because he or she had no way of knowing the safe method of passage, it shall be determined that the subway company, as the manager of a public place, has not fulfilled its duty of safety and security and shall bear corresponding tort liability for the passenger's losses.

full_text_en:
Gao Ziyu v. Nanjing Metro Group Co., Ltd. — dispute over right to health

Ruling Summary

The duty of safety protection is a legal obligation of the manager of a public place or public facility. The person with the duty of safety protection must not only ensure the safety of the place or facility under its management, but also provide necessary warnings, instructions, notifications, and assistance to persons engaging in activities within the place or using the facility, in order to prevent the occurrence of harm. If a metro company primarily controls passenger entry and exit through automatic ticket gates, and it fails to make reasonable arrangements and management for how fare-exempt passengers and their accompanying persons can safely pass through the gates, thereby causing a passenger to be injured when unable to know the safe passage method, then the metro company, as the manager of a public place, shall be deemed to have failed to fulfill its duty of safety protection and shall bear corresponding tort liability for the passenger's losses.

Plaintiff: Gao Ziyu, male, 69 years old, Han ethnicity, residing in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendant: Nanjing Metro Group Co., Ltd., domiciled at Zhongshan Road, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

The plaintiff, Gao Ziyu, filed a lawsuit with the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against the defendant, Nanjing Metro Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as the Metro Company), regarding a dispute over the right to health.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On the afternoon of June 29, 2012, the plaintiff was taking the metro from Xinjiekou Metro Station in Nanjing. While entering the station after swiping his card at the entry gate, the gate suddenly closed, pinching the plaintiff's abdomen, causing a closed abdominal injury, acute peritonitis, and ileal perforation. This incident resulted in the plaintiff's hospitalization, causing him great pain and financial loss. The plaintiff repeatedly negotiated compensation with the defendant Metro Company but failed to reach a settlement. Therefore, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit with the court, requesting an order that the defendant compensate the plaintiff for medical expenses of RMB 36,362.67, nursing fees of RMB 12,000, hospital meal subsidies of RMB 1,060, nutrition fees of RMB 1,800, transportation expenses of RMB 800, disability compensation of RMB 59,354, and moral damages of RMB 10,000.

Defendant's Defense: The plaintiff, Gao Ziyu, accompanied by a child, swiped his card to enter the station. Due to negligence, he accidentally collided with the already-closed gate and was injured. The plaintiff violated the defendant's metro riding regulations, so the defendant bears no liability for the plaintiff's injury. The defendant disputes the amount of some losses claimed by the plaintiff. The defendant requests that the court dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

Facts Found by the Court

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, found the following facts upon trial:

On June 29, 2012, the plaintiff, Gao Ziyu, accompanied by a fare-exempt child, was taking the train at Xinjiekou Metro Station, which is under the defendant Metro Company's management. When the plaintiff swiped his card to enter the station, his abdomen came into contact with the entry gate wing, and he was injured. On the same day, he sought medical treatment at the Nanjing General Hospital of Nanjing Military Command, PLA (hereinafter referred to as the Military General Hospital). The diagnosis was closed abdominal injury, acute diffuse peritonitis, ileal perforation, and other conditions. The plaintiff underwent treatments including a double ileostomy. The plaintiff was treated at the Military General Hospital and Nanjing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, with a total hospitalization of 53 days. After failing to obtain compensation for medical expenses from the defendant, the plaintiff filed this lawsuit.

During the trial, upon the plaintiff's application, the court entrusted the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute to conduct a judicial appraisal of the plaintiff's disability grade, nursing period, and nutrition period. On May 7, 2013, the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute issued a Judicial Appraisal Opinion, concluding that the plaintiff's small intestine resection of less than one-half constituted a Grade 9 disability, the appropriate nursing period was 120 days post-injury, and the appropriate nutrition period was 120 days post-injury.

Issues in Dispute at First Instance

1. Whether the defendant, the Metro Company, should bear compensation liability for the plaintiff Gao Ziyu's injuries.
2. The authenticity of the various expenses incurred by the plaintiff due to this injury.

I. Whether the defendant Metro Company should bear compensation liability for the plaintiff Gao Ziyu's injuries.

The plaintiff, Gao Ziyu, argued that the defendant Metro Company failed to provide proper guidance for the plaintiff's entry into the station. When the plaintiff, accompanied by a fare-exempt child, was passing through the gate normally, he was pinched by the gate. As the owner and manager of the gate, the defendant should bear tort liability.

The plaintiff Gao Ziyu also submitted the following evidence:

1. Surveillance video from June 29, 2012. The video shows the process of the plaintiff Gao Ziyu and the accompanying child swiping their card to enter the station. After the plaintiff swiped the card, the child accompanying him ran through the gate first. The plaintiff followed the child, attempting to pass through the gate but was blocked by the gate wing and immediately stepped back, failing to pass through. Due to the blurry video image, it could only be seen that the plaintiff's abdomen contacted the gate wing; it was indistinguishable whether the wing pinched the plaintiff's body or the plaintiff collided with the wing.

2. A printout of a news report from the Yangzi Evening News dated September 29, 2006, titled "Pregnant Woman Pinched by Gate While Entering Station," which describes a pregnant woman whose abdomen was pinched by the gate due to slow movement.

3. Surveillance video of the gate where the plaintiff was injured on October 16, 2013, obtained by the court upon the plaintiff's application. The video shows an adult and a child entering the station simultaneously. After the adult swiped the card and entered first, the child had not yet fully passed through the wing when the wing closed tightly against the child's head. The plaintiff Gao Ziyu used evidence 2 and 3 to argue that the defendant's gate wings could potentially pinch passengers.

The defendant Metro Company argued that there were notices about riding the metro at every ticket window in the defendant's metro stations, which explicitly prohibit children from entering the station alone. The working principle of the gate in question is that each card swipe causes the gate wing to open and close once. An adult accompanying a child through the metro gate should comply with the requirements of the above notice and the gate's functional specifications. When a passenger accompanies a child to ride the metro normally, as long as they fulfill the most basic duty of supervision over the child, they can safely pass through the metro gate. Evidence 1 shows that when the child accompanying the plaintiff Gao Ziyu exited the gate, the plaintiff had not yet passed through the gate wing. The plaintiff failed to properly supervise the child. After the child passed through the gate alone, the plaintiff, in pursuit of the child, inadvertently collided with the gate. Therefore, the plaintiff's injury was caused by his own negligence, and the defendant should not bear compensation liability for the plaintiff's injury. The defendant disputes the authenticity of evidence 2. The defendant argues that evidence 3 proves that the metro gate does not pinch people and that the situation shown in that video is not similar to the plaintiff's situation and is not comparable.

The defendant Metro Company submitted the following evidence:

1. A wing gate safety statement from Gunnebo Security Systems (China) Co., Ltd., stating that the gates provided by the company for Nanjing Metro Lines 1 and 2 are safe and reliable and will not pinch passengers.

2. The "Nanjing Metro Operation Co., Ltd. Ticket Notice," posted on the side of the ticket window, which stipulates ticket usage, fare adjustments, ticket damage handling, ticket exchange regulations, etc. It includes: one ticket is limited to one person; one adult passenger may bring one child under 1.3 meters in height free of charge to enter the station.

The plaintiff Gao Ziyu disputed the authenticity and relevance of evidence 1. He argued that evidence 2 only described the scope of fare exemption, items to be carried while riding, etc., but did not explain how a child should enter the station accompanied by an adult.

Upon court inspection, the operation method of the defendant Metro Company's entry gate was as follows: after a passenger swipes a ticket, the wing opens; after one passenger passes through, the wing closes.

II. Authenticity of the expenses incurred by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu due to this injury.

1. Medical expenses: RMB 36,362.67. This included amounts paid from the plaintiff Gao Ziyu's medical insurance personal account and out-of-pocket payments, totaling RMB 36,362.67. The defendant Metro Company confirmed this expense.

2. Nursing fees: RMB 12,000. The plaintiff Gao Ziyu claimed RMB 100 per day for 120 days based on the judicial appraisal. The plaintiff submitted nursing fee receipts from Yuan Haishang, Ye Jiangning, etc., totaling RMB 14,740. The plaintiff stated that he hired multiple nursing workers after the injury, the nursing period exceeded 200 days, and the actual daily nursing fee standard was higher than RMB 100. The plaintiff now claims nursing fees of RMB 12,000.

The defendant Metro Company argued that the 120-day nursing period determined by the judicial appraisal opinion was unreasonable and should be calculated as 60 days, with the daily nursing fee standard determined according to law.

3. Hospital meal subsidies: RMB 1,060. The plaintiff Gao Ziyu calculated this based on 53 days of hospitalization at RMB 20 per day. The defendant Metro Company confirmed this expense.

4. Nutrition fees: RMB 1,800. The plaintiff Gao Ziyu calculated this based on the 120-day nutrition period determined by the judicial appraisal at RMB 15 per day.

The defendant Metro Company argued that the 120-day nutrition period determined by the judicial appraisal opinion was unreasonable and should be calculated as 60 days at RMB 15 per day.

5. Transportation expenses: RMB 800.

The plaintiff Gao Ziyu submitted fuel receipts dated July 19, July 26, and July 30, 2012, totaling RMB 790, three taxi receipts, and several parking fee receipts. Some parking fee receipts did not indicate dates. The plaintiff stated that he was transported by taxi or driven by family members for medical treatment, and some transportation receipts were not preserved, so the transportation receipts provided by the plaintiff do not fully correspond one-to-one with the treatment dates.

The defendant Metro Company disputed the authenticity of the evidence and only recognized transportation expenses of RMB 100.

6. Disability compensation: RMB 59,354. The defendant Metro Company confirmed this expense.

7. Moral damages: RMB 10,000.

The defendant Metro Company argued that this expense should be determined by the court according to law.

Judgment

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, held at first instance:

The right to life and health of citizens is protected by law. According to Article 37, paragraph 1 of the Tort Liability Law, if a manager of a public place such as a hotel, shopping mall, bank, station, or entertainment venue fails to fulfill its duty of safety protection, causing harm to another person, it shall bear tort liability. In this case, the defendant Metro Company, as the manager of the metro station and the ticket gates, should fulfill the corresponding duty of safety protection during the process of passengers entering the station to ride the train. It must not only ensure the normal operation of the gates but also provide necessary guidance on how passengers can safely pass through the gates when entering the station and equip corresponding facilities to enable fare-exempt passengers to pass normally. If the defendant's failure to fulfill the above obligations results in passenger injury, it shall bear corresponding tort liability. In this case, the defendant only informed passengers about ticket usage and other ticket matters in the ticket notice but failed to make reasonable arrangements and management for how fare-exempt passengers and their accompanying persons could safely enter the station. This led to the plaintiff Gao Ziyu, when bringing a fare-exempt child and swiping his card to enter, contacting the gate and being injured without being able to know the safe entry method. Therefore, there is a causal relationship between the plaintiff's injury and the defendant's failure to fulfill its duty of safety protection. The defendant should bear corresponding tort liability for the plaintiff's injury. The opening and closing of the metro gate wing is its normal working principle. After the child accompanying the plaintiff passed through the gate when the plaintiff swiped his card and passed the ticket inspection, the plaintiff intended to pass through the gate but failed to carefully observe the closure of the wing, failing to exercise the necessary duty to observe and be careful. Therefore, the plaintiff was negligent with respect to his own injury and should also bear certain responsibility. Considering factors such as the degree of fault of both parties, the court determined that the defendant should bear 70% liability for the plaintiff's injuries, and the plaintiff should bear 30% liability.

Regarding the medical expenses of RMB 36,362.67, hospital meal subsidies of RMB 1,060, and disability compensation of RMB 59,354 incurred by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu due to the injury, the defendant Metro Company did not object, and the court confirmed these amounts.

Regarding the nursing fees claimed by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu, the plaintiff provided evidence showing he hired nursing workers for care. Combined with the nursing period of 120 days post-injury determined by the judicial appraisal opinion, the court of first instance determined the amount as RMB 12,000, calculated at the general local nursing worker daily rate of RMB 100. Although the defendant Metro Company disputed the 120-day nursing period determined by the judicial appraisal, it provided no evidence to support its position. Therefore, the court did not adopt the defendant's argument.

Regarding the nutrition fees claimed by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu, based on the judicial appraisal opinion and the plaintiff's injury condition, the court confirmed the claimed amount of RMB 1,800. Although the defendant Metro Company disputed the 120-day nutrition period determined by the judicial appraisal, it provided no evidence to support its position. Therefore, the court did not adopt the defendant's argument.

Regarding the transportation expenses claimed by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu, according to the law, transportation receipts should correspond with the place, time, number of persons, and number of times of medical treatment. Because the receipts provided by the plaintiff could not prove they were expenses incurred for medical treatment, the court did not confirm the amounts stated on the receipts. Since the defendant Metro Company recognized this expense as RMB 100, the court determined transportation expenses to be RMB 100.

The total of the above expenses was RMB 110,676.67. The defendant Metro Company should bear 70% compensation liability, i.e., compensation of RMB 77,473.67 to the plaintiff Gao Ziyu.

Regarding the moral damages claimed by the plaintiff Gao Ziyu, considering factors such as the plaintiff's disability grade, the location of the disability, and the degree of fault of both parties, the court determined the amount to be RMB 7,000.

Accordingly, pursuant to Article 119 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, Articles 16, 26, and 37(1) of the *Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China*, Articles 17, 19, 21, 22, 23, 24, and 25(1) of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases of Personal Injury Compensation*, and Articles 8(2), 10, and 11 of the *Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Determination of Liability for Moral Damages in Civil Torts*, the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, rendered the following judgment on November 15, 2013:

The defendant, Nanjing Metro Group Co., Ltd., shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate the plaintiff, Gao Ziyu, for medical expenses, nursing fees, nutrition fees, transportation expenses, disability compensation, and moral damages, totaling RMB 84,473.67.

After the first-instance judgment, neither party appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.
